# Recognising risk and knowing when to refer

The four cases below are further simulated-patient encounters in the same format (see the
[*Everyday and preventive counselling*](cases-counselling.qmd) chapter), now with higher stakes. The
patients in that chapter were well or worried-well. With these four, the first job is to notice what is
going wrong: a deficiency, a disease, or a habit that could do harm. Often the safest course is to
recognise the limit of general advice and refer.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The patient is an **AI simulation for practice, not a real person, and not medical advice**.
Treat it as a natural consultation: ask, listen, and agree a realistic plan. If the simulated
patient is unavailable, the encounter notes this and continues.
:::

## Aisha: persistent fatigue

A 24-year-old office worker with months of fatigue, which she puts down to stress. She will
not volunteer much, so draw out what is really going on, explain your concern plainly, and agree
a sensible next step.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-iron-deficiency-aisha.case.yml"></div>

## Mr Chua: unintentional weight loss

A 79-year-old whose daughter noticed his clothes hanging loose. He feels "okay, just tired," and
is quietly proud he has been eating less and plainer. Recognise what the weight loss means, turn
the advice towards eating more, and agree a safe next step.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-frailty-undernutrition-mr-chua.case.yml"></div>

## Mdm Devi: calcium tablets after a wrist fracture

A 63-year-old who broke her wrist in a small fall and now wants to megadose calcium tablets.
Reframe the "more is better" idea, point her to what actually protects bone, and recognise what a
fragility fracture needs.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-bone-fracture-mdm-devi.case.yml"></div>

## Encik Rahman: diet changes in early chronic kidney disease

A 58-year-old with diabetes and hypertension who now has early chronic kidney disease. He has almost
stopped eating protein, drinks star-fruit juice to "detox," and has switched to a "low-sodium" salt
substitute. Undo the harmful ideas, reinforce what is safe, and recognise when to refer.

<div data-island="case" data-src="/cases/sim-ckd-protein-encik-rahman.case.yml"></div>
